en: The *Mahāvaipulya-Adbhuta-sūtra*, "Chapter on Skillful Means," translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven,
Imperially Appointed Grand Officer (Chao Feng Da Fu).

Translated by the Imperial Preceptor and Dharma Master Śīladharma, Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, by Imperial Decree. At that time, there was a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Mahāmati who rose from his seat amidst the assembly, adjusted his robes with solemnity, joined his palms in reverence, prostrated at the feet of the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“How do those who practice as bodhisattvas employ skillful means regarding the objects of the five desires so that they may take them up without attachment, and yet always act without obstruction?
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Great Intention, saying:
“Excellent, excellent!”
"O Mahāmati!
Your name is 'Supreme Vision' and 'Supreme Meaning,' for you are able to ask such a question amidst this assembly.

Those who practice the bodhisattva path and have deeply planted roots of goodness before the Buddhas in future ages—this is what is called skillful means (upāya-kauśalya), by which they are established together with all the Buddhas."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāmati again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How should those who practice the path of the bodhisattva deeply plant roots of goodness in the presence of the Buddhas in future ages?”
"I only pray that the World-Honored One, for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings,
will extensively proclaim and teach it. The Buddha said, "Good son!
Listen attentively now, and I shall explain it for you.

If there is someone who practices even a small portion of giving, yet is able to arouse a superior resolve for the sake of all sentient beings, the merit obtained from that most excellent and wholesome mind is dedicated to all sentient beings; such virtuous benefit is inexhaustible.
It is like rain falling upon the great ocean: the number of individual drops cannot be known, and as they flow in succession, they are without end.

One who practices giving skillfully dedicates all merit to all sentient beings; likewise, all their virtues serve as provisions for all wholesome dharmas, which increase and become ever more excellent, remaining inexhaustible until the perfection of all virtues upon attaining Buddhahood.
"Furthermore, Great Intention!
If there is another person who, upon seeing a place where a maṇḍala is established, offers a single incense, at the time of making this offering they should form this thought:
'May all sentient beings universally attain the supreme fragrance of precepts, be fully endowed with all requisites of happiness, and may all their wishes be fulfilled.'"
“If one offers a single flower, may all sentient beings universally aspire to receive great offerings equally among gods and humans.

If one offers a single lamp, may all sentient beings universally aspire to have their blindness opened, to eliminate all darkness, and to attain great illumination like the light of the sun and moon.”
"If one gives ointments for the purpose of anointing and adorning, may all sentient beings universally attain the mark of a true golden complexion and be adorned with celestial fragrances.
If one gives clothing, may all sentient beings universally be endowed with a sense of shame and dread of blame, and be free from all transgressions."

"If one gives morsel food, may all sentient beings universally attain the samādhi of celestial ambrosia, further obtain the supreme flavor of the Dharma-ambrosia, and be fully endowed with happiness."
"If one gives bells and chimes, may all sentient beings universally attain the most supreme, pure, and wondrous Brahma-voice, bringing joy and satisfaction to all who hear it.
If one gives parasols, may all sentient beings universally be freed from the hardships of wind and rain, attaining great coolness that universally covers all."

"If one gives banners and streamers, one universally vows that the bodies of all sentient beings shall be like the bright moon—pure, clean, and white, with light shining everywhere, beloved and cherished by all people throughout the world."

“If one bestows a precious fly-whisk, may all sentient beings universally be freed from all dust and defilements; may their bodies attain purity and great renown, and may they be fully endowed with the most supreme auspiciousness.”
"If one gives various ornaments, may all sentient beings universally attain the precious, holy ornaments of all the Buddhas' merits.
If one gives songs and music, may all sentient beings universally attain superior faculties of hearing, constantly hearing the wondrous and sublime voices of all Buddhas."
"If one gives boats, ships, and mounts, one universally vows that all sentient beings may attain the Supreme Vehicle.

Furthermore, by giving whatever things sentient beings delight in, one attains the mark of a youth—supple, exquisite, and beautiful—experiences celestial bliss, and finds joy and mastery in all activities."

"If one offers sandalwood incense, one universally prays that all sentient beings may attain the thirty-two marks of a great man, being fully adorned with them up to the invisible crown of the head, from which a wondrous fragrance constantly emanates."
"If one gives a seat, one universally vows that all sentient beings shall enjoy celestial wealth and bliss, and each shall occupy the most supreme and most excellent Great Vajra Seat."
"If one gives bedding and furniture, may all sentient beings universally attain the most supreme joy and contentment.
If one gives monasteries and dwellings, may all sentient beings universally dwell in celestial, delightful, and wondrous jeweled pavilions, fully perfecting the four bases of supernormal power."

"If one gives land that is empty, one universally vows that all sentient beings shall attain stable dwelling in the supreme and wondrous ten stages (bhūmis), and swiftly reach the most exalted and perfect stage of Buddhahood."

"If one gives to one's retinue, one universally prays that all sentient beings shall obtain the constant protection of worldly devas, humans, asuras, and others—protection that is firm, indestructible, most supreme, and most excellent—and that whatever they undertake shall be without equal."

"If one gives medicine, may all sentient beings universally be vowed to be free from all suffering of illness; like a great medicinal tree, may they attain a vajra body that cannot be destroyed, adorned with every ornament, and always experience the most supreme, pleasant joy."
“If one gives a bright mirror, may it be universally prayed that all sentient beings are like the light of the moon, universally illuminating all.
If one gives a vessel, may it be universally prayed that all sentient beings obtain the great vase of the worthy ones, pouring forth the water of the Dharma to universally moisten all.”
"If one gives gardens, groves, and trees, may all sentient beings universally wish that their bodies become like the kalpavṛkṣa tree.
If one gives ghee and curd, may all sentient beings universally wish to obtain the flavor of supreme bliss."
"If one gives sweet and delicious things, one should universally wish that all sentient beings may obtain the most supreme, lovely flavor of light ease and bliss.
Furthermore, when practitioners of the Bodhisattva path see any men, women, or male and female servants, they should give rise to this thought:
'May all sentient beings universally be far removed from the entanglements of affection and the sufferings of grief and affliction, and may each and every one attain sovereign happiness.'"
"If one perceives the realm of suffering, one should give rise to this thought:
'May all sentient beings universally attain liberation from all sufferings, achieving freedom and sovereignty equal to that of all Buddhas.'"

"If one conceives of all sentient beings as one's parents, teachers, and preceptors, and treats them with reverence and respect, then within this very life—whether among gods or humans, or in any place of rebirth such as among śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas—one’s faculties will be disciplined and one will be free from all suffering."
"When dwelling in the pleasures of the five desires, one should give rise to this thought:
'May all sentient beings universally attain their every wish as they desire, and may all fully possess the supreme practices of a bodhisattva.'"
"When bathing, one should give rise to this thought:
'May all sentient beings universally be free from all dust and defilement, pure and unstained, equal to all Buddhas.'"
"When entering gardens, groves, monasteries, or any other place, one should give rise to this thought:
'May all sentient beings universally attain entry into the supreme gateway of the Dharma of liberation.'"
"If one goes out from any place or direction, one should give rise to this thought:
'May all sentient beings universally be vowed to emerge from the limits of saṃsāra and abide in the dharma of peace and bliss.'"
"When eating and drinking, one should give rise to this thought:
'May all sentient beings universally be freed from the evil realms and sever the perception of food and drink.
When among one's retinue, one should give rise to this thought:"
“May all sentient beings universally be free from strife and contention, and may they love and respect one another as spiritual friends, with compassion, peace, and equanimity.
When opening the door, one should give rise to this thought:
“May all sentient beings universally open the gate of liberation and all enter therein.”
"When closing a door, one should universally vow that all sentient beings close the gates to the evil realms and never again enter them.
When treading upon a road, one should give rise to this thought:
'May all sentient beings practice according to the Dharma and proceed in accordance with the true path.'"
"If one is traveling by boat or carriage, one should give rise to this thought:
'May all sentient beings universally ride upon the Supreme Vehicle and ascend the path of perfect enlightenment.'"
"When there is something to be crossed over, one should give rise to this thought:
'May all sentient beings universally be able to transcend the sufferings of the hells and other realms, never again entering them.'"
"When there is any discourse on permanence, one should give rise to this thought:
'May all sentient beings universally attain the manifestation of right mindfulness and the perfection of all dharmas.'"
"If one sees someone giving rise to anger, one should immediately feel joy and form this thought:
'May all sentient beings universally cause all poisonous harms and anger to subside, and may they remain far removed from the disturbances of Māra.'"
"If there are words spoken that proclaim the wholesome Dharma, one should give rise to this thought:
'May all sentient beings universally attain the wisdom of all Buddhas and possess unimpeded eloquence.'"
"In places of jesting, song, music, or chanting, one should give rise to this thought:
'May all sentient beings everywhere always experience great joy, receive all manner of wealth and pleasure, and enjoy sovereign contentment.'"
"When sleeping, one should form this thought:

'May all sentient beings universally give rise to the supreme mind, emerge from the mire of the dust and darkness of ignorance, ensure that all their actions are established by the Buddhas, and abide in perfect wisdom.'"
"When walking in meditation, you should give rise to this thought:
'May all sentient beings everywhere always tread upon the paths of the sages.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāmati, having heard this teaching, felt great joy and again addressed the Buddha, saying:"
“Excellent, World-Honored One!

You have well expounded this Dharma, which enables all practitioners of the bodhisattva path to ensure that their physical, verbal, and mental actions are performed virtuously; it ensures they are always sustained by the protection of all Buddhas, and that all sentient beings in the evil realms receive the Buddha’s salvation.”
“World-Honored One!
Those who practice the bodhisattva path in the future final age should act according to the skillful means as taught by the Buddha; this is precisely what is called practicing the bodhisattva path.”
The Buddha said: “Great Intention! It is so, it is so.”
If those who practice the bodhisattva path train in this way, they will attain firm faith that no longer regresses, and their seeds, being fully complete, will give rise to manifest activity.
In general, you should know that this is what is called the supreme characteristic of a bodhisattva, and it is also the most excellent skillful means.
You all should diligently practice this true Dharma and expound it for others.

At that time, having heard the Buddha preach this Dharma, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahāmati rejoiced and praised him, prostrated at the feet of the World-Honored One, and withdrew to stand to one side.
The Chapter on Skillful Means from the *Buddhabhāṣita-mahāvaipulya-acintya-sūtra* (The Great Vaipulya Sutra of Inconceivable Profundity Spoken by the Buddha)
